title: Tidy Tuesday 1
text:
pixar_data <- pixar_films |>
  left_join(public_response, by = "film")


ggplot(pixar_data, aes(x = release_date, y = run_time))+
  geom_point(color= "navy")+
  labs(x = "Release Date", y="Run Time min", title = "Pixar Films Release Date and Run Times")

title: Pixar Movies - Tidy Tuesday 1
text:
Intro
Everyone loves a good Pixar movie. You go as a kid, you go as a parent, you go as a college student who misses the innocence and nostalgia that Pixar movies inspire. But why does it feel like every movie is so darn long these days? Let’s explore that through a plot.

pixar_data <- pixar_films |>
  left_join(public_response, by = "film")


ggplot(pixar_data, aes(x = release_date, y = run_time))+
  geom_point()+
  labs(x = "Release Date", y="Run Time min", title = "Pixar Films Release Date and Run Times")









Data Source
Data for this visualization was accessed through the TidyTuesday Pixar Films dataset.
Original data:
Leung, Eric. pixarfilms: An R Data Package to Explore Pixar Films, the People, and Reception Data. Data provided mostly in part by Wikipedia.

title: Taylor Swift - Tidy Tuesday 2
text:
The world has grown up along side Taylor Swift, and with that, her music has changed. Here is a visualization of her songs relationship to loudness and danceability. Each point represents a song and each color represents one of her albums. This data set was made in 2023 so it includes her songs and albums up to that date.
ggplot(Taylor_Swift, aes(x = loudness, y = danceability, color = album_name))+
  geom_point()+
  scale_color_taylor_d() +
  labs(x = "Loudness", y="Danceability", title = "Taylor Swift Danceability", color = "Album")

title: Taylor Swift - Tidy Tuesday 2
